definition_zh: 每年的；一年一次的；全年的；年刊
definition_en: happening once every year, calculated over a period of one year, or a book published once a year
core_image: 桌上摊开的一叠年度报表
scene: 年终大会上，财务把一叠报表放在桌上。The company publishes an annual report every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 annual 是「年度的」（第 2 个义项：按一整年计算或覆盖一整年）；句意是公司每年春天发布年度报告。

pos.zh: 形容词：每年的；一年一次的；全年的
名词：年刊；年鉴；一年生植物

名词：周年纪念日，同源于拉丁语「年」

senses.title: Happening once a year
senses.definition: happening, done, or produced once every year
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生、进行或产出一次的
senses.example: The village holds an annual fair in September.
senses.exampleCN: 村里每年九月举办一次集市。
senses.why: Annual is the adjective from Latin annus, 'year', so it marks the thing that comes round once in that cycle.
senses.whyCN: annual 是拉丁语 annus「年」的形容词，因此用来标示在那个周期里出现一次的事物。

senses.title: Calculated over a year
senses.definition: measured over or covering a full year, as with income, leave, or growth
senses.definitionCN: 按整年计算或涵盖整年的，如收入、假期或增长率
senses.example: The company publishes an annual report every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公司每年春天发布年度报告。
senses.why: The year is also a unit of measurement, so annual can mean the total for one year rather than an event inside it.
senses.whyCN: 年也可以是一个计量单位，所以 annual 能表示一整年的总额，而不是一年中发生的某件事。

senses.title: A yearly publication
senses.definition: a book, magazine, or collection published once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版一次的书籍、杂志或作品集
senses.example: She bought the school annual as a souvenir.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了学校年刊留作纪念。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective of time into a noun for the thing that appears in that time, as with daily and monthly.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示时间的形容词转成名词，指在那个时间出现的东西，daily 与 monthly 都是如此。

intro.en: Annual comes straight from the Latin word for year.
intro.cn: annual 直接来自拉丁语中表示「年」的词。

items.cn: annus 意为「年」，也是 anniversary 与 annuity 的词基。

items.en: annualis was the adjective meaning 'yearly'.
items.cn: annualis 意为「每年的」，是形容词形式。

items.en: Old French anuel carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 anuel 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English annual first described religious observances held once a year.
items.cn: 英语 annual 最初指每年举行一次的宗教仪式。

items.en: The noun sense 'yearbook' appeared later, in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词义「年刊」出现较晚，在十九世纪。

definition_zh: 每年；一年一次地；按年度计算地
definition_en: once every year, or in a way that is calculated over each year
core_image: 日历上被圈起来的同一个月份
scene: 董事会固定在三月碰头，桌上摆着去年的账本。The committee meets annually in March.
sceneCN: 这里 annually 是「每年一次地」（第 1 个义项：每年发生一次）；句意是委员会每年三月开会。

senses.title: Once every year
senses.definition: at intervals of one year, of an event that repeats
senses.definitionCN: 以一年为间隔，用于重复发生的事件
senses.example: The committee meets annually in March.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每年三月开会。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective of year into an adverb of frequency, so annually answers the question how often.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示「年」的形容词变成频率副词，所以 annually 回答的是「多久一次」。

senses.title: Calculated year by year
senses.definition: in a way that is measured or revised for each year, as with figures or rates
senses.definitionCN: 以每一年为单位进行计量或调整，如数字或比率
senses.example: Interest is compounded annually, not monthly.
senses.exampleCN: 利息按年复利计算，而不是按月。
senses.why: The same adverb can mark the unit of calculation rather than the frequency of an event, since the year is both a cycle and a measure.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词也能标示计算单位而不只是事件频率，因为年既是周期也是量度单位。

intro.en: Annually is the adjective annual with -ly added, and the year root stays visible.
intro.cn: annually 是形容词 annual 加 -ly 构成，表示「年」的词根仍然清晰。

items.en: annus meant 'year'.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」。

items.en: annualis meant 'yearly'.
items.cn: annualis 意为「每年的」。

items.en: English borrowed annual as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语借入 annual，兼作形容词与名词。

items.en: The adverb annually was formed with the native suffix -ly.
items.cn: 副词 annually 由本族语词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: Annually now also marks yearly calculation in finance and statistics.
items.cn: 现代 annually 还用于金融与统计中的按年计算。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the year root; the near-meaning group is other frequency adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享「年」词根；近义组是其他频率副词。

normalIntro.en: Annual plus -ly gives the adverb of frequency.
normalIntro.cn: annual 加 -ly 构成频率副词。

normal.en: Annual is the adjective; add -ly for the adverb.
normal.cn: annual 是形容词，加 -ly 得到副词。

normal.en: Annually answers how often, not how long.
normal.cn: annually 回答「多久一次」，不回答「持续多久」。

normal.en: Meets annually, held annually, published annually are common.
normal.cn: meets annually、held annually、published annually 都很常见。

normal.en: Do not confuse annually with annally; the u is needed.
normal.cn: 不要漏掉 u，写成 annally 是错的。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-nu-al-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-nu-al-ly。

abstract.cn: 想象墙上日历同一个日期又被圈起来。

abstract.en: See a clock whose hand takes a whole year to return.
abstract.cn: 想象一根要走一整年才回到原位的指针。

abstract.en: See a ledger reopened each January.
abstract.cn: 想象每年一月重新翻开的账本。

examples.cn: 委员会每年三月开会。

examples.en: Interest is compounded annually, not monthly.
examples.cn: 利息按年复利计算，而不是按月。

examples.en: The survey is carried out annually across the country.
examples.cn: 这项调查每年在全国范围内进行一次。

root: 由形容词 annual 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；annual 来自拉丁语 annualis，词根 annus 意为「年」，与 anniversary、annuity 同族。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is frequency, the other is the unit of calculation.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项表示频率，另一个义项表示计算单位。

core.cn: 核心意象：每十二个月闭合一次的圆圈。

intro.cn: 这是一个规则的频率副词，建立在表示「年」的拉丁形容词之上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin year root annus sits inside annual and annually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 annus「年」藏在 annual 与 annually 之中。

definition_zh: 匿名的；无名的；毫无特色的
definition_en: having no name given or known, or lacking any distinctive character
core_image: 信末空着的签名处
scene: 信封里没有落款，只有一张打印的纸。The donation came from an anonymous reader.
sceneCN: 这里 anonymous 是「匿名的」（第 1 个义项：不署名的）；句意是这笔捐款来自一位匿名读者。

pos.zh: 形容词：匿名的；无名的；无特色的

senses.title: With no name given
senses.definition: written, given, or done by someone who does not reveal their name
senses.definitionCN: 由不透露姓名的人所写、所给或所做的
senses.example: The donation came from an anonymous reader.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔捐款来自一位匿名读者。
senses.why: Greek an- means 'without' and onoma means 'name', so anonymous literally describes something that arrives without a name attached.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「无」，onoma 意为「名字」，所以 anonymous 字面就是指送来时没有附上名字的东西。

senses.title: With no known author
senses.definition: used of a work or person whose name is unknown rather than deliberately withheld
senses.definitionCN: 用于作品或人，其名字是不为人知，而非有意隐去
senses.example: The painting was long thought to be by an anonymous artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画长期被认为出自一位无名画家之手。
senses.why: The same word covers both hiding a name and simply not knowing it, because in either case no name is available.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指隐去名字，也指根本不知道名字，因为两种情况下都拿不到名字。

senses.title: Without distinctive character
senses.definition: lacking any feature that would make a place, object, or experience memorable
senses.definitionCN: 缺少任何能让地方、物件或经历留下印象的特点
senses.example: They spent the night in an anonymous hotel near the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在机场附近一家毫无特色的旅馆过了一夜。
senses.why: If a thing has no name you can recall, it feels interchangeable, and that feeling of facelessness is the extended sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西没有你能记住的名字，它就显得可以随便替换，这种面目模糊的感觉就是延伸义。

intro.en: Anonymous is Greek for 'nameless', rebuilt in English from Latin.
intro.cn: anonymous 在希腊语中意为「无名的」，英语中是经由拉丁语重新拼成的。

items.en: onoma meant 'name', the root of many English name-words.
items.cn: onoma 意为「名字」，是许多英语名字类词的词根。

items.en: anonymos meant 'without a name', built with the prefix an-.
items.cn: anonymos 意为「没有名字的」，由前缀 an- 构成。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective almost unchanged.
items.cn: 拉丁语几乎原样接收了这个希腊形容词。

items.en: English anonymous first described books with no author named.
items.cn: 英语 anonymous 最初形容未署作者名的书。

items.en: The sense of 'faceless, without character' developed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 「面目模糊、毫无特色」的义项在二十世纪发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group plays on the name-root; the near-meaning group covers ways of not being identified.
note.cn: 形近组围绕「名字」词根做文章；近义组是各种不被识别的说法。

definition_zh: 另一个；再一个；另一回事
definition_en: one more of the same kind, a different one, or a different matter altogether
core_image: 空杯旁边又摆上一只同样的杯子
scene: 杯子空了，他合上书，又给自己倒了一杯。She finished one chapter and started another.
sceneCN: 这里 another 是「另一个」（第 1 个义项：同类中的另一个）；句意是她读完一章又开始读另一章。

senses.title: A different one
senses.definition: one more person or thing of the same kind, seen as a different individual
senses.definitionCN: 同类中的另一个人或物，被看作不同的个体
senses.example: She finished one chapter and started another.
senses.exampleCN: 她读完一章，又开始读另一章。
senses.why: Another began as an plus other, so it always means one other item, counted separately from the one already mentioned.
senses.whyCN: another 最初写作 an 加 other，因此始终表示「另一个」个体，与前面提到的那个分开计数。

senses.title: One more, added
senses.definition: an additional person or thing, added to those already there
senses.definitionCN: 在已有的之外再增添的一个人或物
senses.example: Would you like another cup of tea?
senses.exampleCN: 你要再来一杯茶吗？
senses.why: Because the second item is counted after the first, another naturally means 'one more' when the kind stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 因为第二件是在第一件之后计数的，所以当种类不变时，another 自然表示「再来一个」。

senses.title: A different matter
senses.titleCN: 另一回事；完全不同的事
senses.definition: used in phrases such as another matter to mark something as a separate issue
senses.definitionCN: 用于 another matter 等短语，表示那是另一件独立的事
senses.example: The price is fine; the delivery time is another matter.
senses.exampleCN: 价格没问题，交货时间则是另一回事。
senses.why: When the second thing is not the same kind at all, another marks a break in the topic rather than more of the same.
senses.whyCN: 当第二件事根本不是同一类时，another 标示的是话题的转换，而不是同类的追加。

intro.en: Another is simply the words an and other run together.
intro.cn: another 就是 an 与 other 两个词连写而成。

items.en: an was the word for 'one', the ancestor of modern a and an.
items.cn: an 是表示「一」的词，是现代 a 与 an 的祖先。

items.en: ōther meant 'the second of two, different'.
items.cn: ōther 意为「两者中的另一个、不同的」。

items.en: The two words were written as a phrase, then joined.
items.cn: 两个词先作为短语使用，随后连写。

items.en: The single word another appears in writing.
items.cn: 连写形式 another 在书面语中出现。

items.en: Another now covers both 'one more' and 'a different matter'.
items.cn: 现代 another 兼指「再来一个」与「另一回事」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the other family; the near-meaning group gives words for addition and difference.
note.cn: 形近组是 other 词族；近义组给出表示追加与差异的词。

pos.zh: 名词：答案；回答；解决办法

derivatives.zh: 形容词：可回答的；负有责任的
动词：回应，是 answer 的拉丁语系近义词

senses.title: To reply to a question
senses.definition: to say or write something in return when someone has asked a question
senses.definitionCN: 当别人提问时，用口头或书面作出回应
senses.example: Nobody could answer the last question.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能回答最后那个问题。
senses.why: Old English andswaru was built from and, 'against', and swerian, 'to swear', so an answer was originally a statement sworn back against a charge; the backtracking motion of reply is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andswaru 由 and「对着」与 swerian「发誓」构成，最初指面对指控时反过来起誓申明，那种「对回去」的动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To solve a problem
senses.definition: to work out the solution to a puzzle, a sum, or a difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 算出谜题、算术题的解法，或解决一个难题
senses.example: She answered the riddle in under a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她不到一分钟就解开了这个谜语。
senses.why: A question and a puzzle both leave a gap that must be filled, so the idea of replying widened from words to solutions.
senses.whyCN: 提问与谜题都会留下一个必须填补的空位，所以 answer 从「用话回应」扩展到「给出解法」。

senses.title: To react to a call or knock
senses.definition: to pick up the phone or go to the door when someone is trying to reach you
senses.definitionCN: 有人打来电话或敲门时，去接或去开
senses.example: He answered the phone before the second ring.
senses.exampleCN: 第二声铃响之前他就接了电话。
senses.why: A ringing phone is a question addressed to the house, and picking it up is the physical form of replying.
senses.whyCN: 响铃的电话像是对着屋子里提出的一个问题，而拿起听筒就是把这个回应做成了动作。

senses.title: To fit or correspond to
senses.definition: to match a description, a need, or a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与某种描述、需要或目的相吻合
senses.example: The room answers the description in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间在每一处细节上都符合描述。
senses.why: If a thing corresponds to what was asked for, it stands as the reply to the expectation, which is why answer can mean 'fit'.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物正好对应所要求的东西，它就等于对那份期待作出了回应，因此 answer 可以表示「符合」。

intro.en: Answer is a native Germanic compound whose two halves once meant 'against' and 'swear'.
intro.cn: answer 是本族日耳曼语复合词，两部分原本分别表示「对着」与「发誓」。

items.en: and meant 'against' or 'in return', not yet the modern conjunction.
items.cn: and 意为「对着」或「作为回报」，还不是现代的那个连词。

items.en: swerian meant 'to swear an oath'.
items.cn: swerian 意为「起誓」。

items.en: andswaru was a sworn statement made against an accusation.
items.cn: andswaru 指面对指控时起誓作出的申辩。

items.en: The word lost its legal flavour and came to mean any reply.
items.cn: 这个词失去法律色彩，泛指任何答复。

items.en: The noun answer and the verb answer split into separate uses, including answering the phone and answering a need.
items.cn: 名词 answer 与动词 answer 分化出多种用法，包括接电话与满足需要。

note.en: The look-alike group is the answer family; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of replying.
note.cn: 形近组是 answer 词族；近义组是其他表示回应的动词。

definition_zh: 预料；预期；期盼；先于……行动
definition_en: to expect something to happen, to look forward to it, or to act before someone else does
core_image: 棋手在对手落子前就摆好了应对的一步
scene: 会开到一半，经理已经在纸上写下可能出现的三种反对意见。We anticipate strong resistance to the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 anticipate 是「预料」（第 1 个义项：预先想到某事会发生）；句意是我们预料这个计划会遇到强烈反对。

pos.zh: 动词：预料；预期；期盼；先于……行动

derivatives.zh: 形容词：预先的；期待性的

senses.title: To expect in advance
senses.definition: to think that something will probably happen and be ready for it
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能会发生，并为此作好准备
senses.example: We anticipate strong resistance to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料这个计划会遇到强烈反对。
senses.why: Latin anticipare joined ante, 'before', to capere, 'take', so the word literally means taking something before it arrives; expecting is that mental pre-taking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anticipare 把 ante「在前」与 capere「拿取」合在一起，字面就是「在事情到达之前先拿住」，预料正是这种在心里的预先拿取。

senses.title: To look forward to
senses.definition: to await something with pleasure or eagerness
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉快或急切的心情等待某事
senses.example: The children anticipate the trip with excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们兴奋地期盼着这次旅行。
senses.why: If you have already taken the future event into your mind, you can begin enjoying it now, and that pleasure turns expectation into looking forward.
senses.whyCN: 如果未来的事已经被你提前拿进心里，你现在就能开始享受它，这种愉悦使「预料」变成了「期盼」。

senses.title: To act before someone
senses.definition: to do something before another person can do it
senses.definitionCN: 在别人能行动之前先做
senses.example: They anticipated their rivals by launching the product a month early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们比对手抢先一个月推出产品。
senses.why: Taking before also works in time, not only in thought: to anticipate a rival is to occupy the position first.
senses.whyCN: 「先拿」不仅发生在思想里，也发生在时间上：anticipate 对手就是把位置先占住。

intro.en: Anticipate is a Latin compound meaning 'to take before'.
intro.cn: anticipate 是拉丁语复合词，意为「先取」。

items.en: ante meant 'before, in front of'.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前方」。

items.en: capere meant 'to take or seize', the source of capture and captive.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿取、抓住」，是 capture 与 captive 的来源。

items.en: anticipare meant 'to take beforehand'.
items.cn: anticipare 意为「预先取得」。

items.en: English anticipate first meant 'to take or use before the proper time'.
items.cn: 英语 anticipate 最初意为「在适当时间之前取得或使用」。

items.en: The modern senses of expecting and looking forward grew from the older idea of being ahead.
items.cn: 现代「预料」与「期盼」的义项都从「走在前面」这个较早的观念发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin take- root; the near-meaning group holds words for seeing ahead.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「拿取」词根；近义组是表示预见未来的词。

definition_zh: 古董；古物；古老的；古董的
definition_en: an object from an earlier period valued for its age, or an adjective describing such objects
core_image: 旧货店里落着薄尘的黄铜座钟
scene: 街角的小店摆满旧家具，铜器泛着暗光。She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
sceneCN: 这里 antique 是「古董的」（第 2 个义项：形容年代久远且有价值的物品）；句意是她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语 antiquus
形容词：研究古物（收藏）的

senses.title: An object from the past
senses.definition: a piece of furniture, jewellery, or other object that is old and valued for its age
senses.definitionCN: 年代久远、因年代而受珍视的家具、首饰或其他物件
senses.example: She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。
senses.why: Latin antiquus meant 'former, ancient', and the noun use in English picked out objects that survive from that former time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antiquus 意为「从前的、古老的」，英语里的名词用法挑出的就是从那个从前留存下来的物件。

senses.title: Belonging to an earlier period
senses.definition: used of furniture, objects, or styles that come from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 用于来自较早时代的家具、物件或样式
senses.example: The room was full of antique furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆满了古董家具。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain temporal meaning of antiquus, so anything surviving from an earlier age can be called antique.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 antiquus 单纯的时间含义，因此任何从较早年代留存下来的东西都能叫 antique。

senses.title: Old-fashioned, out of date
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way for ideas or methods that belong to the past
senses.definitionCN: 略带嘲意地指属于过去的思想或方法
senses.example: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。
senses.why: Once a thing is old enough to be quaint, the same word can belittle an idea as a museum piece.
senses.whyCN: 当一样东西旧到显得古怪时，同一个词也能把某种观念贬为博物馆里的陈列品。

definition_zh: 焦虑；忧虑；担心；渴望
definition_en: an uneasy feeling about something uncertain, a strong wish to do something well, or a medical condition of excessive worry
core_image: 深夜盯着天花板，心里反复盘算明天的事
scene: 考试前一夜，他翻来覆去，脑子里全是没复习到的章节。Her anxiety about the exam kept her awake.
sceneCN: 这里 anxiety 是「焦虑」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事的担忧）；句意是对考试的焦虑让她睡不着。

pos.zh: 名词：焦虑；忧虑；担心；渴望

senses.title: A feeling of worry
senses.definition: an uneasy feeling caused by uncertainty about what may happen
senses.definitionCN: 因不确定将会发生什么而产生的不安
senses.example: Her anxiety about the exam kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 对考试的焦虑让她睡不着。
senses.why: Latin anxietas came from anxius, 'choked, uneasy', which itself came from angere, 'to squeeze or strangle'; anxiety is literally a tightening in the chest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anxietas 来自 anxius「被扼住、不安的」，而 anxius 又来自 angere「挤压、扼住」；所以 anxiety 字面上就是胸口被收紧的感觉。

senses.title: A strong wish to do well
senses.definition: an eager but uneasy wish to please someone or to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 急于讨好某人或把事情做好，却又带着不安的心情
senses.example: He waited with anxiety to hear the judges' decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他急切不安地等着听评委的决定。
senses.why: The same tightening happens when you badly want an outcome, so the word covers eager longing as well as fear.
senses.whyCN: 当你非常想要某个结果时，胸口也会同样收紧，所以这个词既指恐惧也指急切的渴望。

senses.title: A medical condition
senses.definition: a clinical condition marked by persistent and excessive worry
senses.definitionCN: 以持续而过度的担忧为特征的临床病症
senses.example: She was treated for anxiety after months of sleeplessness.
senses.exampleCN: 失眠数月之后，她因焦虑症接受治疗。
senses.why: When the ordinary tightening becomes constant and disabling, the same noun is used as the name of the disorder.
senses.whyCN: 当这种普通的紧绷变得持续且影响生活时，同一个名词就被用来命名这种病症。

intro.en: Anxiety goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to squeeze'.
intro.cn: anxiety 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「挤压」的动词。

items.cn: angere 意为「挤压、使窒息、折磨」。

items.cn: anxius 形容一种被扼住、不安的心理状态。

items.cn: anxietas 是表示痛苦与忧虑的名词。

items.cn: 英语 anxiety 最初指烦扰不安的状态。

items.en: In the twentieth century anxiety also became the clinical name for a treatable disorder.
items.cn: 二十世纪，anxiety 又成为可治疗的焦虑症的临床名称。

definition_zh: 焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried about something uncertain, or very eager to do or get something
core_image: 候诊室里捏皱的挂号单
scene: 手术室外的走廊上，家属一遍遍看墙上的钟。The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anxious 是「焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事感到担忧）；句意是随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。

pos.zh: 形容词：焦虑的；担忧的；渴望的

senses.title: Worried about something
senses.definition: feeling uneasy because you do not know how something will turn out
senses.definitionCN: 因为不知道事情会怎样发展而感到不安
senses.example: The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
senses.exampleCN: 随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。
senses.why: The Latin ancestor angere meant 'to squeeze', and anxius described a person whose chest feels constricted; anxious keeps that bodily tightness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 angere 意为「挤压」，anxius 形容胸口发紧的人；anxious 保留了这种身体上的紧绷感。

senses.title: Very eager to do something
senses.definition: wanting very much to do something or for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常想做某事，或非常希望某事发生
senses.example: She was anxious to finish the report before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她急于在中午前完成报告。
senses.why: Strong desire tightens the mind in much the same way as fear, so anxious for and anxious to express eagerness rather than dread.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的愿望让心里绷紧的方式与恐惧相似，所以 anxious for 与 anxious to 表达的是急切而不是害怕。

intro.en: Anxious is the adjective built on the Latin root for a tightened chest.
intro.cn: anxious 是建立在拉丁语「胸口收紧」词根上的形容词。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze or choke'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压、使窒息」。

items.en: anxius meant 'uneasy, distressed'.
items.cn: anxius 意为「不安的、苦恼的」。

items.en: The noun anxietas named the state of worry.
items.cn: 名词 anxietas 指忧虑的状态。

items.en: English anxious first meant 'greatly troubled'.
items.cn: 英语 anxious 最初意为「极为烦恼的」。

items.en: The sense of eager desire became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「急切渴望」的义项在十九世纪变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Latin anxiety family; the near-meaning group gives other worried words.
note.cn: 形近组同属拉丁语焦虑词族；近义组是其他表示担忧的词。

normalIntro.en: Anxious is a squeezed chest, whether from fear or from wanting.
normalIntro.cn: anxious 是收紧的胸口，可能因为害怕，也可能因为渴望。

normal.en: Anxious about a problem, anxious to do something.
normal.cn: 对问题用 anxious about，急于做事用 anxious to。

normal.en: The noun is anxiety, not anxiousness in most writing.
normal.cn: 多数书面语中名词用 anxiety，而不用 anxiousness。

normal.en: Anxious for news means waiting eagerly for it.
normal.cn: anxious for news 意为急切等待消息。

normal.en: The x sounds like ks: ANK-shus.
normal.cn: x 读作 ks 的音：ANK-shus。

normal.en: Do not confuse anxious with anger; the root is shared but the meaning is not.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 anger 混为一谈，词根相关但含义不同。

abstract.en: See a crumpled ticket in a waiting room.
abstract.cn: 想象候诊室里被捏皱的单据。

abstract.en: See eyes fixed on a corridor clock.
abstract.cn: 想象盯着走廊时钟的眼睛。

abstract.en: See a hand raised long before the question ends.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没说完就举起的手。

examples.en: The family grew anxious as the hours passed.
examples.cn: 随着时间过去，家属越来越焦虑。

examples.en: She was anxious to finish the report before noon.
examples.cn: 她急于在中午前完成报告。

examples.en: He felt anxious about the interview all week.
examples.cn: 整整一周他都在为面试担忧。

root: 来自拉丁语 anxius「不安的」，源于 angere「挤压、扼住」，与 anxiety、anguish 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The same tightness serves fear about the future and eagerness for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种紧绷既用于对未来的恐惧，也用于对未来的渴望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand crushing a waiting-room ticket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把候诊单攥皱。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of tension that still carries a physical feel.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示紧绷的拉丁形容词，至今仍带着身体感。

latinIntro.en: The squeeze root angere underlies anxious, anxiety, and anguish.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「挤压」的词根 angere 贯穿 anxious、anxiety 与 anguish。

definition_zh: 焦虑地；担忧地；急切地
definition_en: in a worried and uneasy way, or with eager impatience
core_image: 不停朝门口张望的脚步
scene: 车晚点了，站台上的人一次次探头看铁轨尽头。She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
sceneCN: 这里 anxiously 是「焦急地」（第 1 个义项：带着担忧地做某事）；句意是她焦急地等着晚点的火车。

pos.zh: 副词：焦虑地；担忧地；急切地

senses.title: In a worried way
senses.definition: in a manner that shows unease about what may happen
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出对可能发生之事不安的方式
senses.example: She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
senses.exampleCN: 她焦急地等着晚点的火车。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective of inner tension into a description of how a person acts while that tension is showing.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示内心紧绷的形容词变成描述动作的方式，也就是把这种紧绷表现给人看时的样子。

senses.title: With eager impatience
senses.definition: in a way that shows strong eagerness for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈盼望某事发生的方式
senses.example: He anxiously checked the results page every few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他每隔几分钟就急切地刷新成绩页面。
senses.why: Since anxious can mean eager, the adverb also describes hurried, impatient action rather than fear.
senses.whyCN: 既然 anxious 可以表示渴望，这个副词也用来描述匆忙而不耐烦的举动，而不是恐惧。

intro.en: Anxiously is anxious plus the native adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: anxiously 是 anxious 加本族语副词词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压」。

items.en: anxius meant 'uneasy'.
items.cn: anxius 意为「不安的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词。

items.en: The adverb anxiously was formed with -ly.
items.cn: 副词 anxiously 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: It now covers both worried waiting and eager checking.
items.cn: 现代用法兼指焦虑的等待与急切的查看。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anxiety family; the near-meaning group gives other adverbs of unease.
note.cn: 形近组是焦虑词族；近义组是其他表示不安的副词。

normalIntro.en: Anxiously shows the tight feeling in the way someone moves.
normalIntro.cn: anxiously 把紧绷的感觉表现在动作里。

normal.en: Anxious is the adjective; add -ly for the adverb.
normal.cn: anxious 是形容词，加 -ly 得到副词。

normal.en: Wait anxiously and ask anxiously are the commonest pairs.
normal.cn: wait anxiously 与 ask anxiously 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The adverb can mean eagerly, not only fearfully.
normal.cn: 这个副词也能表示急切，不只是害怕。

normal.en: Keep the x sound: ANK-shus-ly.
normal.cn: 保留 x 的读音：ANK-shus-ly。

normal.en: Do not write anxiouslly; there is only one l before y.
normal.cn: 不要写成 anxiouslly，y 前只有一个 l。

abstract.en: See footsteps turning at every sound.
abstract.cn: 想象每有声响就转身的脚步。

abstract.en: See a head leaning out over a platform edge.
abstract.cn: 想象有人探出头望向站台尽头。

abstract.en: See a page refreshed again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象页面被反复刷新。

examples.en: She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
examples.cn: 她焦急地等着晚点的火车。

examples.en: He anxiously checked the results page every few minutes.
examples.cn: 他每隔几分钟就急切地刷新成绩页面。

examples.en: The mother looked anxiously at the sleeping child.
examples.cn: 母亲不安地看着熟睡的孩子。

root: 由形容词 anxious 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；anxious 源于拉丁语 anxius「不安的」，再上溯到 angere「挤压」。

sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词同时覆盖焦虑的等待与急切的查看。

intro.cn: 这是一个规则的 -ly 副词，建立在表示紧绷的拉丁形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin squeeze root appears inside anxious and anxiety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「挤压」词根藏在 anxious 与 anxiety 之中。

definition_zh: 任何；一些（用于疑问、否定）；丝毫；任何一个
definition_en: one or some, no matter which, used in questions and negatives, or emphasising a small amount
core_image: 一排一模一样的抽屉，随便拉开哪个都行
scene: 冰箱里几乎空了，主人摊开手问客人想喝点什么。Do you have any milk left?
sceneCN: 这里 any 是「一些」（第 1 个义项：用于疑问句中表示不确定的数量）；句意是你还有牛奶吗？

senses.title: Some, in questions and negatives
senses.titleCN: 一些；任何（用于疑问与否定）
senses.definition: an unspecified amount or number, used when asking or denying
senses.definitionCN: 不确定的数量或数目，用于提问或否定
senses.example: Do you have any milk left?
senses.exampleCN: 你还有牛奶吗？
senses.why: Old English ǣnig was literally 'one' with the suffix -ig, so any started as 'a single one' and widened to an unspecified amount.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ǣnig 字面就是「一」加词尾 -ig，因此 any 从「单个一个」扩展为不确定的数量。

senses.title: Whichever one you choose
senses.definition: used to say that one from a group will do, because the choice does not matter
senses.definitionCN: 表示某一组里的任意一个都行，因为选哪个都无所谓
senses.example: Take any seat you like.
senses.exampleCN: 你随便坐哪个座位都行。
senses.why: Once any means 'one, it does not matter which', it naturally expresses free choice among a set.
senses.whyCN: 当 any 表示「随便哪个都行」时，它自然就表达了一组事物中的自由选择。

senses.title: At all, in the least
senses.definition: used with comparatives or negatives to emphasise even a small degree
senses.definitionCN: 与比较级或否定词连用，强调哪怕一点点程度
senses.example: The situation is not any better today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的情况一点也没好转。
senses.why: If even one small amount is in question, the word can stress a minimum degree, which is how the adverb use arose.
senses.whyCN: 如果连很小的量都成问题，这个词就能强调最低程度，副词用法正是这样产生的。

intro.en: Any began as a word for 'one' and slowly loosened into 'some or whichever'.
intro.cn: any 最初表示「一个」，后来逐渐松弛为「一些、随便哪个」。

items.en: ān meant 'one', the ancestor of a, an, and one.
items.cn: ān 意为「一」，是 a、an 与 one 的祖先。

items.en: ǣnig meant 'any one' and was used in questions and negations.
items.cn: ǣnig 意为「任何一个」，用于疑问与否定。

items.en: The form settled as any and spread to all kinds of choice.
items.cn: 形式固定为 any，并扩展到各种选择。

items.en: The adverbial use with comparatives appeared, as in any better.
items.cn: 与比较级连用的副词用法出现，如 any better。

items.en: Any now works as determiner, pronoun, and adverb.
items.cn: 现代 any 兼作限定词、代词与副词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the any- family; the near-meaning group gives other quantity words.
note.cn: 形近组是 any 构成的词族；近义组是其他数量词。

entries.definition: an unspecified amount, used in statements

normalIntro.en: Any is 'one' opened up to every possible choice.
normalIntro.cn: any 就是把「一个」打开成所有可能的选择。

normal.en: Use any in questions and negatives, some in plain statements.
normal.cn: 疑问句与否定句用 any，肯定陈述用 some。

normal.en: Any plus one, thing, body, where builds a whole family.
normal.cn: any 加 one、thing、body、where 构成一整族词。

normal.en: Any longer means no longer in negative sentences.
normal.cn: 否定句里 any longer 意为「不再」。

normal.en: In any case is a fixed phrase meaning whatever happens.
normal.cn: in any case 是固定短语，意为无论如何。

normal.en: Any is unstressed in most sentences: EN-ee at most.
normal.cn: any 在多数句子里不重读，最多轻读第一个音节。

abstract.en: See a hand sweeping across a row of identical drawers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扫过一排一模一样的抽屉。

abstract.en: See an empty fridge with one shelf bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一台空空如也的冰箱。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing at no particular door.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指随随便便指向某扇门。

examples.en: Do you have any milk left?
examples.cn: 你还有牛奶吗？

examples.en: Take any seat you like.
examples.cn: 你随便坐哪个座位都行。

examples.en: The situation is not any better today.
examples.cn: 今天的情况一点也没好转。

root: 古英语 ǣnig 由 ān「一」加词尾 -ig 构成，本义「任何一个」，后扩展为表示不确定数量、自由选择与强调程度。

sensesIntro.en: From 'one of them' come the quantity use, the free-choice use, and the emphatic adverb.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「其中任意一个」发展出数量用法、自由选择用法与强调副词。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在一排相同的抽屉上方徘徊。

intro.cn: 这是一个本族数量词，与 one、thing、body、where 组合成庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Any is Germanic in origin, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: any 源自日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 任何人；随便哪个人；要人
definition_en: any person at all, used in questions and negatives, or an important person
core_image: 敞开的门口，谁都可以走进来
scene: 门口没有名单，也没有保安，礼堂的门就那么开着。Anybody can join the club.
sceneCN: 这里 anybody 是「任何人」（第 1 个义项：无论哪个人都包括）；句意是任何人都能加入这个社团。

pos.zh: 代词：任何人；随便哪个人

derivatives.zh: 代词：任何人，与 anybody 基本同义
代词：没有人，是 anybody 的否定对应词

senses.title: Any person at all
senses.definition: used in questions and negatives to mean one person, it does not matter who
senses.definitionCN: 用于疑问句与否定句，指某个人，是谁都无所谓
senses.example: Anybody can join the club.
senses.exampleCN: 任何人都能加入这个社团。
senses.why: Any supplies 'whichever' and body here is the old word for a person, so anybody is literally 'any person'.
senses.whyCN: any 提供「随便哪个」，body 在这里是古语中「人」的意思，所以 anybody 字面就是「任何一个人」。

senses.title: A person of importance
senses.definition: used in the phrase anybody who is anybody, meaning all the important people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 anybody who is anybody 这一说法，指所有重要人物
senses.example: Anybody who is anybody was at the opening night.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜，所有有头有脸的人都到了。
senses.why: If anybody means every person without exception, then 'anybody who is anybody' narrows it to those who count, giving the ironic sense of a VIP.
senses.whyCN: 既然 anybody 指毫无例外的每个人，那么 anybody who is anybody 就把它收窄为「算得上人物的人」，于是产生了「要人」的讽刺意味。

intro.en: Anybody is any joined to body in its old sense of 'person'.
intro.cn: anybody 是 any 与旧义为「人」的 body 组合而成。

items.en: ǣnig meant 'any one'.
items.cn: ǣnig 意为「任何一个」。

items.en: bodig meant 'body', and by extension a living person.
items.cn: bodig 意为「身体」，引申为活人。

items.en: Any body was written as two words meaning 'any person'.
items.cn: any body 分写为两个词，意为「任何人」。

items.en: The compound anybody appears as a single pronoun.
items.cn: 复合代词 anybody 以连写形式出现。

items.en: The idiom anybody who is anybody gave the word its 'important person' use.
items.cn: 习语 anybody who is anybody 赋予这个词「要人」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the any- family; the near-meaning group is other indefinite pronouns for people.
note.cn: 形近组是 any 词族；近义组是其他指人的不定代词。

normalIntro.en: Anybody is any plus body, an old way of saying person.
normalIntro.cn: anybody 就是 any 加 body，而 body 是「人」的旧说法。

normal.en: Anybody is singular: anybody knows, not anybody know.
normal.cn: anybody 作单数：anybody knows，不用 know。

normal.en: Use anybody in questions and negatives, somebody in statements.
normal.cn: 疑问与否定用 anybody，肯定陈述用 somebody。

normal.en: Anybody else means other people besides those mentioned.
normal.cn: anybody else 指除了已提到的人之外的人。

normal.en: It takes a singular pronoun in formal writing: anybody and his bag.
normal.cn: 正式书面语中回指用单数代词。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-y-bod-y.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-y-bod-y。

abstract.en: See an open door with no guest list.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有名单的门。

abstract.en: See a room filling with every kind of person.
abstract.cn: 想象房里坐满各种各样的人。

abstract.en: See a velvet rope lifted for the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象为人群抬起的丝绒围栏。

examples.en: Anybody can join the club.
examples.cn: 任何人都能加入这个社团。

examples.en: Anybody who is anybody was at the opening night.
examples.cn: 首演之夜，所有有头有脸的人都到了。

examples.en: Did anybody see where the keys went?
examples.cn: 有人看见钥匙去哪儿了吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: any（任何）加 body（人）：任何人。

root: 由 any「任何」与 body「身体、人」组合而成，中古英语时期分写，十六世纪后连写为不定代词；与 anyone 基本同义。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is every person without exception; the idiom turns it into the select few who matter.

senses.title: In spite of that

senses.title: Any object or matter

senses.title: In spite of that
senses.definition: used when something happens despite a reason against it
senses.definitionCN: 在存在相反理由的情况下某事仍然发生
senses.example: It was late, but she stayed anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 时间很晚了，但她还是留了下来。
senses.why: Any means 'whichever' and way means 'route or manner', so anyway began as 'by any route'; going by any route means going despite obstacles.
senses.whyCN: any 意为「随便哪个」，way 意为「路线或方式」，所以 anyway 本义是「走哪条路都行」；哪条路都走，也就是有阻碍也照走。

senses.title: Adding a further point
senses.definition: used to add a supporting remark or to return to the main topic
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充一个理由，或把话题拉回正题
senses.example: It is too expensive, and anyway we do not need it.
senses.exampleCN: 太贵了，而且我们也不需要它。
senses.why: If the outcome holds by any route, the speaker can add another reason without changing the conclusion, which produces the 'besides' use.
senses.whyCN: 如果无论走哪条路结论都成立，说话人就能再加一个理由而不改变结论，于是产生了「况且」的用法。

senses.title: To change or close a topic
senses.definition: used in speech to signal a return to the subject or the end of a digression
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于示意回到主题或结束题外话
senses.example: Anyway, let us get back to the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 总之，我们回到预算上来吧。
senses.why: The 'in spite of that' force can also brush aside the previous digression, so anyway works as a topic hinge in conversation.
senses.whyCN: 「尽管如此」的力量也能把前面的题外话一扫而过，所以 anyway 在对话里成了转换话题的铰链。

definition_zh: 分开；相隔；除了；拆散
definition_en: separated by distance or space, into pieces, or not included in something
core_image: 两只原本并排的杯子被推到桌子两端
scene: 吵架之后，两个人一前一后走，中间隔着好几步。They sat apart and said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 apart 是「分开地」（第 1 个义项：彼此隔开一段距离）；句意是他们分开坐着，一言不发。

derivatives.zh: 名词：种族隔离，字面即「分开的状态」
名词：公寓，指分隔出的居住单元
名词：部分，是 apart 的词根

senses.title: Separated by space
senses.definition: at a distance from one another rather than together
senses.definitionCN: 彼此相隔一段距离，而不是在一起
senses.example: They sat apart and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分开坐着，一言不发。
senses.why: The a- here is a worn form of on, and part means a portion, so apart pictures things placed on their own separate portions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 是 on 的弱化形式，part 意为「部分」，所以 apart 描绘的是各自占着一部分、彼此不相连。

senses.title: Into pieces
senses.definition: used with verbs such as take or fall to show something separating into its parts
senses.definitionCN: 与 take、fall 等动词连用，表示事物分成若干部分
senses.example: He took the clock apart to repair it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钟拆开来修理。
senses.why: If the whole is split into its parts, the parts stand apart, so the word moves from distance to dismantling.
senses.whyCN: 如果整体被分成各个部分，这些部分就彼此分开了，于是这个词从「有距离」过渡到「拆解」。

senses.title: Not counting something
senses.definition: used in apart from to mean except for or as well as
senses.definitionCN: 用于 apart from，表示「除了……之外」
senses.example: Apart from the noise, the flat is perfect.
senses.exampleCN: 除了吵一点，这套房子很完美。
senses.why: Something set apart from the rest is left out of the group, which is exactly the logic of 'except'.
senses.whyCN: 被从其余事物中分开的东西就是被排除在外的，这正是「除外」的逻辑。

intro.en: Apart is the phrase on part, meaning 'into separate parts', fused into one word.
intro.cn: apart 由短语 on part「分成各自的部分」融合成词。

items.cn: pars 意为「部分」，是 part 的来源。

items.en: On part meant 'into parts, separately'.
items.cn: on part 意为「分成部分、各自地」。

items.en: The two words fused and the n was lost before the p.
items.cn: 两个词融合，n 在 p 前脱落。

items.en: Apart now covers distance, dismantling, and exception.
items.cn: 现代 apart 涵盖距离、拆解与除外三种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the part root; the near-meaning group gives other words of separation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 part 词根；近义组是其他表示分离的词。

definition_zh: 公寓；一套住房；房间
definition_en: a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a larger building
core_image: 同一栋楼里被墙隔开的一户户人家
scene: 傍晚的楼道里，每扇门后都亮着不同的灯。They rented a small apartment near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 apartment 是「公寓」（第 1 个义项：楼内一套独立的居住房间）；句意是他们在车站附近租了一套小公寓。

senses.title: A set of rooms to live in
senses.definition: a group of rooms used as a home, usually within a larger building
senses.definitionCN: 用作住所的一组房间，通常位于较大的建筑内
senses.example: They rented a small apartment near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近租了一套小公寓。
senses.why: French appartement came from appartement, 'a separation', because the rooms are a portion set apart inside one building.
senses.whyCN: 法语 appartement 来自意为「分隔」的词，因为这套房间就是在一栋楼里被单独分出来的一部分。

senses.title: A room or suite in a large house

senses.example: The family kept a private apartment on the upper floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这户人家在楼上保留着一套私人房间。
senses.why: Before the modern flat, apartment simply named any set of rooms marked off for one person's use, however grand the house.

definition_zh: 道歉；谢罪；辩白
definition_en: to say that you are sorry for something you have done, or to defend something in speech
core_image: 低着头把一句「对不起」说出口
scene: 他不小心撞翻了别人的咖啡，立刻放下手里的书。She apologized for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 apologize 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：为过错表示歉意）；句意是她为迟到道歉。

senses.title: To say you are sorry
senses.definition: to tell someone that you regret something you did that upset them
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方你为做过并令其不快的事感到抱歉
senses.example: She apologized for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她为迟到道歉。
senses.why: Greek apologia was a speech in defence, built from apo, 'away', and logos, 'word'; the English verb first meant 'to speak in defence' and only later narrowed to owning a fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 apologia 是为自己辩护的言辞，由 apo「离开」与 logos「言辞」构成；英语动词最初意为「出言辩护」，后来才收窄为承认过失。

senses.title: To defend in writing or speech
senses.definition: to argue formally for a belief or a person, a use now mostly found in apologetics
senses.definitionCN: 正式地为某种信念或某人辩护，今多见于护教学语境
senses.example: The essay apologizes for the old custom rather than attacking it.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章是在为旧习俗辩护，而不是抨击它。
senses.why: The older defensive sense survives in apologist and apologetics, where the speaker is explaining a position rather than saying sorry.
senses.whyCN: 较早的辩护义保留在 apologist 与 apologetics 里，那里说话人是在解释一种立场，而不是在道歉。

intro.en: Apologize descends from a Greek word for a speech made in defence.

items.cn: 英语 apology 最初指辩护，而非认错。

items.cn: 动词 apologize 转向表示歉意这一日常含义。

note.cn: 形近组是 apology 词族；近义组是其他承认过失的说法。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的
definition_en: easy to see or understand, or seeming true without being so
core_image: 水面上露出的冰山一角
scene: 会议室的空气一下子僵住，谁都看得出出了问题。It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看出来）；句意是显然出了什么问题。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: Clearly visible or understood
senses.definition: easy to notice or understand from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据证据很容易被察觉或理解
senses.example: It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 显然出了什么问题。
senses.why: Latin apparere meant 'to come into view', built from ad, 'to', and parere, 'to appear'; what is apparent has come into sight.

senses.title: Seeming rather than real
senses.definition: true as far as one can see, but possibly not in fact

senses.example: The apparent calm hid a great deal of anger.
senses.exampleCN: 表面上的平静掩藏着极大的愤怒。
senses.why: Because appearing is not the same as being, apparent can warn that the surface may deceive.

definition_zh: 显然地；看来；据说
definition_en: as it seems from what is known, or according to what people say
core_image: 听到消息后挑起的眉毛
scene: 同事凑过来小声说了一个传闻，说完还补了一句「听说是这样」。Apparently, the meeting has been cancelled.

derivatives.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: As far as one can see
senses.definition: used to say that something seems true from the available evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有证据，某事看起来是真的
senses.example: The two problems are apparently unrelated.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个问题看来并不相关。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective of visibility into a comment on how things look from where the speaker stands.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示可见的形容词变成对「从说话人位置看上去如何」的评注。

senses.title: According to what people say
senses.definition: used to report something you have heard but cannot confirm
senses.definitionCN: 用来转述你听到但无法证实的事
senses.example: Apparently, the meeting has been cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 据说会议取消了。
senses.why: If a fact is apparent to others but not to you, the adverb naturally marks hearsay rather than direct knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事对别人明显而对你并不明显，这个副词自然就标示道听途说而非亲身确证。

items.en: apparere meant 'to become visible'.

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century.

normal.cn: apparent 是形容词，apparently 是副词。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence it usually means 'I have heard'.

normal.en: Apparently so and apparently not are common short replies.

normal.en: It softens a claim: apparently simple means only seemingly simple.

abstract.en: See a question mark drawn beside a fact.

examples.cn: 这两个问题看来并不相关。

examples.en: Apparently, the meeting has been cancelled.

examples.cn: 她显然是不告而别的。

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；吸引
definition_en: to make an urgent request, to ask a court to change a decision, or to be attractive to someone
core_image: 人群前举起的一只求助的手
scene: 洪水过后，村长站在废墟前向外界求援。The village appealed for food and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：紧急请求帮助）；句意是村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。

pos.zh: 动词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；有吸引力

senses.title: To ask urgently for help
senses.definition: to ask strongly and publicly for something needed
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地请求所需之物
senses.example: The village appealed for food and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin appellare meant 'to address, call upon', from ad, 'to', and pellere, 'to drive'; an appeal drives words toward someone who can act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appellare 意为「向……讲话、呼唤」，由 ad「向」与 pellere「推动」构成；appeal 就是把话推向能行动的人。

senses.title: To ask a court to reconsider
senses.definition: to take a legal decision to a higher court for review
senses.definitionCN: 把法律裁决提交上级法院复审
senses.example: They appealed against the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对判决提出上诉。
senses.why: The idea of calling upon a higher authority fits the courtroom: the losing side calls on a higher court.
senses.whyCN: 「向更高权威求助」的观念正适用于法庭：败诉一方向更高一级法院发出请求。

senses.title: To be attractive
senses.definition: to please or interest someone, often because it suits their needs
senses.definitionCN: 使人喜欢或感兴趣，常因契合其需要
senses.example: The simple design appeals to young buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 简洁的设计吸引了年轻买家。
senses.why: Something that appeals to you calls out to your taste, so the word moved from a spoken request to a silent attraction.
senses.whyCN: appeal to 你的东西是在向你的品味发出呼唤，所以这个词从口头请求延伸为无声的吸引。

definition_zh: 出现；露面；显得；出庭
definition_en: to come into sight, to seem a certain way, or to be present in public or in court
core_image: 舞台幕布拉开，演员走到灯光下
scene: 观众等了几秒，幕布一开，主角从侧幕走出来。A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 appear 是「出现」（第 1 个义项：进入视线）；句意是一个身影出现在走廊尽头。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: To come into sight
senses.definition: to become visible or present where someone can see you
senses.definitionCN: 变得可见，或出现在别人能看到的地方
senses.example: A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一个身影出现在走廊尽头。
senses.why: Latin apparere joined ad, 'to', and parere, 'to come forth', so appear is a thing stepping into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」合成，所以 appear 就是某物走进视野。

senses.title: To seem a certain way
senses.definition: to give a particular impression, often without being so in fact
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，而事实上未必如此
senses.example: The task appears easier than it is.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务看起来比实际容易。
senses.why: What steps into view is what we judge by, so appear came to mean 'look like' rather than simply 'be present'.
senses.whyCN: 走进视野的东西正是我们判断的依据，所以 appear 从「在场」转为「看起来像」。

senses.title: To be present officially
senses.definition: to attend a court, a hearing, or a public event as required
senses.definitionCN: 按要求出席法庭、听证会或公开活动
senses.example: He must appear before the judge on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 他必须在周一出庭面见法官。
senses.why: A court requires the person to show themselves in the room, which is the plainest form of appearing.
senses.whyCN: 法庭要求当事人亲自出现在庭上，这正是 appear 最朴素的形态。

definition_zh: 出现；露面；外观；外表
definition_en: the act of coming into sight or being present, or the way someone or something looks
core_image: 镜子前整理衣领的人
scene: 面试前，他对着玻璃门检查自己的衬衫和头发。Her appearance was neat and professional.
sceneCN: 这里 appearance 是「外表」（第 2 个义项：人或物呈现出的样子）；句意是她的外表整洁而专业。

pos.zh: 名词：出现；露面；外观；外表

derivatives.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: The act of appearing
senses.definition: the act of arriving or being seen in public
senses.definitionCN: 到达或在公众场合被看见的行为
senses.example: The singer made a brief appearance on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手在台上短暂露面。
senses.why: The -ance ending turns the verb of coming into view into the event of that coming.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ance 把「进入视野」的动词变成这一事件本身。

senses.title: The way something looks
senses.definition: the visible form or impression that a person or thing gives
senses.definitionCN: 人或物呈现出来的可见形态或给人的印象
senses.example: Her appearance was neat and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的外表整洁而专业。
senses.why: What has appeared is also what we judge by, so the noun shifted from the event to the visible result.
senses.whyCN: 显现出来的东西也是我们判断的依据，于是名词从「事件」转向「可见的结果」。

senses.title: A formal presence in court
senses.definition: the presence of a party before a court or official body
senses.definitionCN: 当事人出现在法庭或官方机构面前
senses.example: His appearance in court lasted only ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的出庭只持续了十分钟。
senses.why: The legal use keeps the plain sense of showing oneself, but fixes it to a required occasion.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留了「亲自现身」的本义，只是把它固定在必须出席的场合。

intro.en: Appearance is the noun made from appear, with the Latin root still visible.
intro.cn: appearance 是由 appear 构成的名词，拉丁词根仍然可见。

items.en: parere meant 'to come forth'.
items.cn: parere 意为「出现」。

items.en: apparere meant 'to become visible'.
items.cn: apparere 意为「显现」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 动词在十三世纪进入英语。

items.en: The noun appearance named the act of coming into sight.
items.cn: 名词 appearance 指进入视野的行为。

items.en: The sense of outward look became the dominant everyday use.
items.cn: 「外观」义成为日常最主要的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the appear root; the near-meaning group gives other words for looks and presence.
note.cn: 形近组共享 appear 词根；近义组是其他表示外观与现身的词。

normal.en: Make an appearance means attend briefly.
normal.cn: make an appearance 意为短暂露面。

normal.en: Physical appearance is the common formal phrase for looks.
normal.cn: physical appearance 是「外貌」的正式说法。

normal.en: To all appearances means judging only by the outside.
normal.cn: to all appearances 意为仅从外表判断。

normal.en: The plural appearances often refers to public performances.
normal.cn: 复数 appearances 常指公开演出场次。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPEAR-ance.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPEAR-ance。

abstract.en: See a collar straightened in a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象镜前整理好的衣领。

abstract.en: See a spotlight finding one person.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯找到一个人。

abstract.en: See a name read out in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上被念到的名字。

examples.en: The singer made a brief appearance on stage.
examples.cn: 这位歌手在台上短暂露面。

examples.en: Her appearance was neat and professional.

dict_mnemonic.text: appear（出现）加 -ance（名词）：出现的样子，外观。

root: 由动词 appear 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；appear 源于拉丁语 apparere「显现」，词根 parere 意为「出现」。

sensesIntro.en: The event of showing up, the look produced by it, and the required court presence.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person checked over in a mirror before entering.
core.cn: 核心意象：进门之前在镜前检视自己的人。

intro.en: A regular noun of the appear family, very productive in English.
intro.cn: 这是 appear 词族中的规则名词，在英语中构词力很强。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root parere, 'to appear', runs through the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 parere「出现」贯穿整个词族。

definition_zh: 食欲；胃口；欲望；兴趣
definition_en: a natural desire for food, or a strong interest in something
core_image: 闻到厨房香味时咽下的口水
scene: 锅盖一掀，热气冲上脸，他立刻觉得饿了。The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
sceneCN: 这里 appetite 是「食欲」（第 1 个义项：对食物的自然欲望）；句意是面包的香味让他有了食欲。

senses.title: A desire for food
senses.definition: the natural feeling that makes you want to eat
senses.definitionCN: 使人想吃东西的自然感觉
senses.example: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。
senses.why: Latin appetitus came from appetere, 'to seek after', built from ad, 'to', and petere, 'to seek'; hunger is the body seeking food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appetitus 来自 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；饥饿就是身体在追寻食物。

senses.title: A strong interest in something
senses.definition: a keen desire for an activity, a challenge, or a type of experience
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、挑战或某种体验的强烈渴望
senses.example: She has an appetite for risk.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢冒险。
senses.why: The seeking after food widened to any object the mind reaches for, so appetite can name ambition or curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 对食物的追寻扩展到心里想抓取的任何对象，所以 appetite 也能指抱负或好奇心。

intro.en: Appetite goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to seek after'.
intro.cn: appetite 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「追寻」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: petere meant 'to seek, aim at'.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、瞄准」。

items.en: appetere meant 'to reach for, desire'.
items.cn: appetere 意为「伸手去取、渴望」。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The figurative sense of desiring challenges or knowledge became common.
items.cn: 渴望挑战或知识的比喻义变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the seek root; the near-meaning group gives other words for desire.
note.cn: 形近组共享「寻求」词根；近义组是其他表示欲望的词。

entries.definition: a small dish before a meal
a contest, from the same seeking verb

normalIntro.en: Appetite is the body or mind reaching out for something.
normalIntro.cn: appetite 就是身体或心思向外伸出去抓某样东西。

normal.en: Lose one's appetite and a good appetite are opposite fixed pairs.
normal.cn: lose one's appetite 与 a good appetite 是相反的两个固定搭配。

normal.en: An appetite for risk means a taste for it.
normal.cn: an appetite for risk 意为喜欢冒险。

normal.en: Whet one's appetite means make someone want more.
normal.cn: whet one's appetite 意为吊起胃口。

normal.en: Appetizer is the small dish that starts a meal.
normal.cn: appetizer 是开胃的头盘。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AP-pe-tite.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AP-pe-tite。

abstract.en: See steam rising from a covered pot.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖下冒出的热气。

abstract.en: See a hand reach toward a bread basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向面包篮。

abstract.en: See a climber eyeing a high wall.
abstract.cn: 想象攀爬者盯着高墙。

examples.en: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
examples.cn: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。

examples.en: She has an appetite for risk.
examples.cn: 她喜欢冒险。

examples.en: He lost his appetite after the long journey.
examples.cn: 长途旅行之后他没了胃口。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 pet（寻求）加 -ite：向食物伸出去的欲望，食欲。

root: 来自拉丁语 appetitus，源于 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；同根词有 appetizing、appetizer，另有 compete、petition。

sensesIntro.en: Seeking food and seeking experience are the same reaching motion.
sensesIntro.cn: 追寻食物与追寻体验，是同一个向外伸手的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving toward food before the mind decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在脑子决定之前已伸向食物。

intro.en: A Latin noun of seeking that English applies to food and to ambition.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示追寻的拉丁名词，英语中兼指食物与抱负。

latinIntro.en: The root petere, 'to seek', also gives petition and compete.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 petere「寻求」也派生出 petition 与 compete。

definition_zh: 掌声；喝彩；赞许
definition_en: the sound of many people clapping to show approval, or praise for an achievement
core_image: 剧场里忽然响起的一整片掌声
scene: 最后一个音落下，灯亮起，观众一齐抬起手。The audience burst into applause.
sceneCN: 这里 applause 是「掌声」（第 1 个义项：观众拍手表示的赞许）；句意是观众爆发出掌声。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：似乎合理的，与 applause 同源于「拍手」

senses.title: Clapping to show approval
senses.definition: the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands in praise
senses.definitionCN: 一群人拍手表示赞赏所发出的声音
senses.example: The audience burst into applause.
senses.exampleCN: 观众爆发出掌声。
senses.why: Latin applaudere joined ad, 'to', and plaudere, 'to clap', so applause is literally clapping toward a performer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applaudere 由 ad「向」与 plaudere「拍手」构成，所以 applause 字面就是朝表演者拍手。

senses.title: Public praise
senses.definition: spoken or written approval for a person's achievement
senses.definitionCN: 对某人成就的口头或书面赞许
senses.example: The policy won applause from both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策赢得了双方的赞许。
senses.why: Clapping is approval made audible, so the same noun can name approval even when no hands are moving.
senses.whyCN: 鼓掌是听得见的赞许，所以同一个名词也能指无人拍手时的赞同。

intro.en: Applause comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to clap towards'.
intro.cn: applause 来自拉丁语中意为「朝……拍手」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: plaudere meant 'to clap the hands'.
items.cn: plaudere 意为「拍手」。

items.en: applaudere meant 'to clap in approval'.
items.cn: applaudere 意为「拍手表示赞许」。

items.en: applausus was the noun for the clapping itself.
items.cn: applausus 是表示拍手这一行为的名词。

items.en: English applause kept the noun while the verb became applaud.
items.cn: 英语保留名词 applause，动词则作 applaud。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the clap root; the near-meaning group gives other signs of approval.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拍手」词根；近义组是其他表示赞许的方式。

entries.definition: seeming reasonable, from the same clap
entries.definitionCN: 似乎合理的，同源于「拍手」

entries.definition: to burst out, from clapping off a stage
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸，同源于「拍手赶下台」

normalIntro.en: Applause is clapping sent toward the stage.
normalIntro.cn: applause 就是朝舞台送去的拍手声。

normal.en: A round of applause is one burst of clapping.
normal.cn: a round of applause 指一阵掌声。

normal.en: The verb is applaud; applause is the noun.
normal.cn: 动词是 applaud，名词是 applause。

normal.en: Thunderous applause describes very loud clapping.
normal.cn: thunderous applause 形容极响的掌声。

normal.en: Applause is uncountable: say a round of applause, not an applause.
normal.cn: applause 不可数，应说 a round of applause，不说 an applause。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPLAUSE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPLAUSE。

abstract.en: See a hall of raised hands in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一片举起的手。

abstract.en: See a conductor turning to bow.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥转身鞠躬。

abstract.en: See a curtain call under warm lights.
abstract.cn: 想象暖光下的谢幕。

examples.en: The audience burst into applause.
examples.cn: 观众爆发出掌声。

examples.en: The policy won applause from both sides.
examples.cn: 这项政策赢得了双方的赞许。

examples.en: She waited for the applause to die down.
examples.cn: 她等着掌声平息下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 plaud（拍手）：朝台上拍手，就是掌声。

root: 来自拉丁语 applausus，源于 applaudere「拍手赞许」，由 ad「向」与 plaudere「拍手」构成；动词形式为 applaud。

sensesIntro.en: Audible clapping and spoken approval are two forms of the same praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 听得见的拍手与说出口的赞许，是同一种赞赏的两种形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands striking together at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手同时拍响。

intro.en: A Latin noun of clapping, with a matching verb that English also uses.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示拍手的拉丁名词，英语另有对应的动词。

latinIntro.en: The root plaudere, 'to clap', also gives plausible and explode.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 plaudere「拍手」也派生出 plausible 与 explode。

definition_zh: 苹果；苹果树
definition_en: a round fruit with firm white flesh and a green, red, or yellow skin
core_image: 果盘里一只红苹果，表皮还带着水珠
scene: 早餐桌上摆着面包、牛奶，还有一只洗干净的苹果。She sliced an apple for the child.
sceneCN: 这里 apple 是「苹果」（第 1 个义项：这种圆形果实）；句意是她给孩子切了一只苹果。

senses.title: The round fruit
senses.definition: a firm round fruit that grows on a tree and is eaten raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 长在树上、可生吃或烹煮的坚实圆形果实
senses.example: She sliced an apple for the child.
senses.exampleCN: 她给孩子切了一只苹果。
senses.why: Old English æppel meant simply 'apple' and could name any fruit; over time it narrowed to the one fruit we now mean.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 æppel 本义就是「苹果」，也能泛指果实；后来才收窄为今天这一种水果。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: used in compounds such as apple tree for the tree itself
senses.definitionCN: 用于 apple tree 等复合词，指苹果树本身
senses.example: An old apple stands at the garden's edge.
senses.exampleCN: 花园边上立着一棵老苹果树。
senses.why: English often uses the fruit name for the plant, as with cherry and plum, so apple can stand for the tree in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用果实名代指植物，樱桃与李子都是如此，所以在复合词里 apple 可以指树。

intro.en: Apple is an old Germanic word that once covered fruit in general.
intro.cn: apple 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，曾泛指各种果实。

items.en: The reconstructed root meant 'apple' and possibly any tree fruit.
items.cn: 重构词根意为「苹果」，也可能泛指树上的果实。

items.en: æppel was the ordinary word for apple and for fruit.
items.cn: æppel 是「苹果」及「果实」的常用词。

items.en: The form shifted toward the modern apple.
items.cn: 词形逐渐演变为现代形式。

items.en: Recipes show apple used specifically for the orchard fruit.
items.cn: 食谱文献显示 apple 已专指果园里的那种水果。

items.en: The word now also appears in many fixed phrases and compounds.
items.cn: 现代这个词还出现在许多固定短语与复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group is orchard fruit; the near-meaning group is other round fruits.
note.cn: 形近组是果园水果；近义组是其他圆形水果。

a sweet fruit with a narrow top

normalIntro.en: Apple is one short word with a very long history.
normalIntro.cn: apple 是一个很短的词，却有很长的历史。

normal.en: An apple a day keeps the doctor away is a well-known saying.
normal.cn: 「每天一苹果，医生远离我」是著名谚语。

normal.en: Apple pie is the classic compound.
normal.cn: apple pie 是最经典的复合词。

normal.en: The apple of one's eye means a much-loved person.
normal.cn: the apple of one's eye 意为掌上明珠。

normal.en: In compounds the fruit name can mean the tree: apple tree.
normal.cn: 复合词里果实名可指树：apple tree。

normal.en: The plural is apples, with a voiced s.
normal.cn: 复数是 apples，s 读浊音。

abstract.en: See a red apple with water still on the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象红苹果表皮还挂着水珠。

abstract.en: See a knife curling a strip of peel.
abstract.cn: 想象小刀削出一圈果皮。

abstract.en: See a branch bent low with fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象被果实压弯的树枝。

examples.en: She sliced an apple for the child.
examples.cn: 她给孩子切了一只苹果。

examples.en: An old apple stands at the garden's edge.
examples.cn: 花园边上立着一棵老苹果树。

examples.en: He packed an apple and a sandwich for lunch.
examples.cn: 他装了一只苹果和一个三明治当午饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap 加 ple：一口咬下去脆生生，就是苹果。

root: 古英语 æppel 源自原始日耳曼语，本可泛指果实，后专指苹果；同族词有 pineapple、apple pie 等复合形式。

sensesIntro.en: The fruit and, in compounds, the tree that bears it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一是指果实，二是在复合词中指结出果实的树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round fruit held in the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心托着的一只圆果。

intro.en: A native Germanic word that forms many compounds.
intro.cn: 这是一个本族日耳曼语词，能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Apple is Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.

definition_zh: 家用电器；器具；装置
definition_en: a machine or device used in the home or workplace for a particular job
core_image: 厨房台面上一排插着电的机器
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱里装的都是电饭锅、熨斗这类东西。The kitchen is fitted with modern appliances.
sceneCN: 这里 appliance 是「家用电器」（第 1 个义项：家中使用的机器设备）；句意是厨房配了现代化电器。

pos.zh: 名词：家用电器；器具；装置

derivatives.zh: 动词：应用；申请，与 appliance 同根

senses.title: A household machine
senses.definition: an electrical machine used in the home, such as a fridge or a washing machine
senses.definitionCN: 家中使用的电器，如冰箱或洗衣机
senses.example: The kitchen is fitted with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房配了现代化电器。
senses.why: The word comes from apply, 'to put to use', so an appliance is a thing applied to a practical task.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 apply「应用」，所以 appliance 就是被用来完成某项实用任务的物件。

senses.title: A device for a specific job
senses.definition: any apparatus designed for a particular purpose, not only in the home
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的设计的任何器械，不限于家庭
senses.example: Dental appliances must be cleaned daily.
senses.exampleCN: 牙科矫治器必须每天清洁。
senses.why: If the word names anything put to a use, it can cover medical and industrial devices as well as kitchen machines.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指任何被投入使用的东西，那么它就能涵盖医疗器械与工业装置，而不只是厨房机器。

intro.en: Appliance is built on the verb apply, with the sense 'something applied to a task'.
intro.cn: appliance 建立在动词 apply 之上，意为「被用于某项任务的东西」。

items.en: applicare meant 'to fold to, attach'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「贴上去、附着」。

items.en: aplier gave English the verb apply.
items.cn: aplier 给英语带来了动词 apply。

items.en: Appliance first meant the act of applying.
items.cn: appliance 最初指「应用」这一行为。

items.en: The sense shifted to the thing applied, especially a device.
items.cn: 词义转向被应用的物件，尤指器械。

items.en: In the twentieth century it narrowed mainly to household machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪它主要收窄为家用机器。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words for equipment.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示设备的词。

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（应用）加 -ance（名词）：拿来用的东西，器具。

root: 由动词 apply 加名词词尾 -ance 构成；apply 源于拉丁语 applicare「贴上、附着」，因此 appliance 本义是「被应用的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Any device applied to a practical job, from kitchen machines to dental fittings.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何被用于实际任务的装置，从厨房机器到牙科矫治器。

intro.en: A noun built on apply, one of the most productive Latin verbs in English.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在 apply 之上的名词，而 apply 是英语中构词力最强的拉丁动词之一。

latinIntro.en: The root applicare, 'to attach', underlies the whole apply family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 applicare「附着」支撑着整个 apply 词族。

items.meaning: a device applied to a task
a thing made for a purpose

definition_zh: 适用的；可应用的；相关的
definition_en: able to be applied to a situation, or relevant to a particular case
core_image: 一块正好扣上卡口的盖板
scene: 律师翻到条款最后一页，确认它是否适用于这起纠纷。The rule is applicable to all members.
sceneCN: 这里 applicable 是「适用的」（第 1 个义项：能套用到某种情形上）；句意是这条规则适用于所有成员。

pos.zh: 形容词：适用的；可应用的

senses.title: Able to be applied
senses.definition: able to be used in a particular situation or to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 能够用于特定情形或特定对象
senses.example: The rule is applicable to all members.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于所有成员。
senses.why: Applicable is apply plus -able, literally 'able to be applied', so it asks whether a rule or method fits the case.
senses.whyCN: applicable 是 apply 加 -able，字面即「可以被应用的」，因此它问的是规则或方法是否对得上这个情形。

senses.title: Relevant to the matter
senses.definition: directly connected with the subject being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 与正在讨论的主题直接相关
senses.example: Please attach any applicable documents.
senses.exampleCN: 请附上任何相关文件。
senses.why: If something can be applied to the case, it belongs to the case, which is how the word also comes to mean relevant.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物能套用到这个案子上，它就属于这个案子，于是这个词也有了「相关」的意思。

intro.en: Applicable is the adjective of apply, meaning 'able to be put to use'.
intro.cn: applicable 是 apply 的形容词，意为「可以被投入使用的」。

items.en: plicare meant 'to fold'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」。

items.en: applicare meant 'to fold to, attach'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「贴上去、附着」。

items.en: English apply developed the sense 'to put to use'.
items.cn: 英语 apply 发展出「应用」的含义。

items.en: Applicable was formed with the suffix -able.
items.cn: applicable 由词尾 -able 构成。

items.en: The word is now standard in legal and technical writing.
items.cn: 现代这个词在法律与技术写作中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words of relevance.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示相关性的词。

normalIntro.en: Applicable asks: can this rule be laid onto this case?
normalIntro.cn: applicable 问的是：这条规则能扣到这个案子上吗？

normal.en: Applicable to is the standard preposition pair.
normal.cn: applicable to 是标准介词搭配。

normal.en: Where applicable appears often in forms and contracts.
normal.cn: where applicable 常见于表格与合同。

normal.en: The noun applicability is more formal than applicable.
normal.cn: 名词 applicability 比 applicable 更正式。

normal.en: The American stress falls on the first syllable: AP-pli-ca-ble.
normal.cn: 美式重音落在第一个音节：AP-pli-ca-ble。

normal.en: Do not confuse applicable with applied; one is a fit, the other is an action.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 applicable 与 applied，一个表示契合，一个表示动作。

abstract.en: See a cover snapping into a matching slot.
abstract.cn: 想象盖板正好扣进卡槽。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto the right form.
abstract.cn: 想象印章盖在正确的表格上。

abstract.en: See a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象只在一把锁里转得动的钥匙。

examples.cn: 这条规则适用于所有成员。

examples.cn: 请附上任何相关文件。

examples.en: The discount is applicable only in June.
examples.cn: 这项折扣只在六月适用。

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（应用）加 -able（可……的）：可以应用的，适用的。

root: 由动词 apply 加形容词词尾 -able 构成；apply 源于拉丁语 applicare「贴上、附着」，故本义为「可以被贴上去的」。

sensesIntro.en: Being able to be applied and being relevant to the case are two sides of one fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 「能被应用」与「与本案相关」是同一契合关系的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part that fits exactly into its slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：恰好嵌入卡槽的部件。

intro.en: An -able adjective on the apply root, common in rules and contracts.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在 apply 词根上的 -able 形容词，常见于规则与合同。

latinIntro.en: The root plicare, 'to fold', also gives complicate and explicit.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 plicare「折叠」也派生出 complicate 与 explicit。

definition_zh: 申请人；求职者；报名者
definition_en: a person who formally asks for a job, a place, or a service
core_image: 手里捏着一叠材料站在窗口前的人
scene: 招聘会门口排着队，每个人都拿着简历。Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 applicant 是「申请人；求职者」（第 1 个义项：正式提出申请的人）；句意是每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。

pos.zh: 名词：申请人；求职者；报名者

collocations.zh: 把申请人列入候选名单

senses.title: A person who applies for a job
senses.definition: someone who formally asks to be considered for a post or a place
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求被考虑录用或录取的人
senses.example: Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。
senses.why: Applicant is the person noun from apply, with -ant marking the one who performs the action of applying.
senses.whyCN: applicant 是 apply 派生的指人名词，词尾 -ant 标示执行「申请」这一动作的人。

senses.title: A person making a formal request
senses.definition: someone who applies for a document, a benefit, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为某种证件、补助或服务提出申请的人
senses.example: The visa applicant must bring two photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 签证申请人必须带两张照片。
senses.why: The same -ant person noun serves every kind of formal request, not only employment.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ant 指人名词适用于各种正式请求，不只用于求职。

intro.en: Applicant is apply plus the Latin person ending -ant.
intro.cn: applicant 是 apply 加拉丁语指人词尾 -ant。

items.en: applicare meant 'to attach oneself to'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「使自己附着于」。

items.en: applicans was the present participle, 'one attaching himself'.
items.cn: applicans 是现在分词，意为「使自己靠近的人」。

items.en: English applicant first meant a person who applies for something.
items.cn: 英语 applicant 最初指为某事提出申请的人。

items.en: With modern employment it became the standard word for a job seeker.
items.cn: 随着现代就业制度，它成为求职者的标准说法。

items.en: The word now covers visas, grants, and school places as well.
items.cn: 现代它还涵盖签证、补助与入学名额。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words for people who seek something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示寻求者身份的词。

entries.definition: a person competing for a post
a person put forward for a role

normalIntro.en: An applicant is the -ant person who does the applying.
normalIntro.cn: applicant 就是执行 apply 这个动作的 -ant 指人名词。

normal.en: Applicant for a post, applicant to a school.
normal.cn: 职位用 applicant for，学校用 applicant to。

normal.en: Job applicant is the most common pair.
normal.cn: job applicant 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not confuse applicant with application; one is a person, the other a form.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 applicant 与 application，一个是人，一个是表格。

normal.en: The plural applicants is regular.

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AP-pli-cant.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AP-pli-cant。

abstract.cn: 想象拿着材料夹排队的人。

abstract.en: See a desk with a name called out.
abstract.cn: 想象桌前有人被叫到名字。

abstract.en: See a stamp landing on a form.
abstract.cn: 想象印章落在表格上。

examples.en: Each applicant was interviewed for ten minutes.
examples.cn: 每位申请人都面谈了十分钟。

examples.en: The visa applicant must bring two photographs.

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（申请）加 -ant（人）：提出申请的人。

root: 由 apply 加拉丁语指人词尾 -ant 构成，源自拉丁语 applicans「使自己靠近的人」；apply 的词根为 plicare「折叠」。

sensesIntro.en: One person noun covers job seekers and anyone else making a formal request.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个指人名词既指求职者，也指任何提出正式申请的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stepping forward with papers in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：拿着材料走上前的人。

latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -ant 标示动作执行者，如 applicant 与 claimant。

definition_zh: 申请；申请书；应用；涂抹；专注
definition_en: a formal request, the act of putting something to use, a substance spread on a surface, or close attention
core_image: 一份填好并贴上照片的表格
scene: 他把简历和表格装进信封，写上面试单位的地址。Her application arrived before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 application 是「申请（书）」（第 1 个义项：正式的书面请求）；句意是她的申请在截止日期前寄到了。

pos.zh: 名词：申请；应用；涂抹；专注

senses.title: A formal request
senses.definition: a written or spoken request for a job, a place, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额或服务提出的书面或口头请求
senses.example: Her application arrived before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她的申请在截止日期前寄到了。
senses.why: Application is the noun of apply, and the oldest formal sense is the act of asking, which then named the papers carrying the request.
senses.whyCN: application 是 apply 的名词，最早的正式义就是「提出请求」这一行为，之后又指承载请求的文件。

senses.title: The act of putting to use
senses.definition: the use of an idea, method, or substance in a practical situation
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、方法或物质用于实际情形
senses.example: The application of this theory is not simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论的应用并不简单。
senses.why: To apply is literally to lay something onto a surface, so application keeps the image of a method being laid onto a problem.
senses.whyCN: apply 字面就是把某物贴到一个表面上，所以 application 保留了「把方法贴到问题上」的意象。

senses.title: A substance spread on
senses.definition: a quantity of cream, paint, or medicine put onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上的一定量的乳霜、颜料或药物
senses.example: A thin application of oil will protect the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄涂一层油可以保护木材。
senses.why: The physical sense of laying something on survives in this concrete use of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 把东西贴上去的物理含义，在这个具体的名词用法中保留下来。

senses.title: Close attention to a task
senses.definition: the quality of giving steady attention to work or study
senses.definitionCN: 对工作或学习持续投入注意力的品质
senses.example: Success here depends on steady application.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的成功取决于持续的专注。
senses.why: If the mind is applied to a task, it is bent onto it, and that effort became a sense of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果心思被「贴」在任务上，就是弯着身子扑在上面，这种用力成了名词的一个义项。

items.en: English application first meant the act of applying.

items.en: The sense of a written request became the most common in everyday use.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other request and use words.

entries.definition: to request or put to use
the act of asking for something

normalIntro.en: Application is the noun of apply in all its senses.

normal.en: Fill in an application, make an application, submit an application.

normal.en: Application form is the paper; application is also the act.
normal.cn: application form 是表格，application 也可指申请行为。

normal.en: The application of a method means putting it to work.
normal.cn: the application of a method 意为把方法投入使用。

normal.en: Steady application means hard, focused work.
normal.cn: steady application 意为持续专注的努力。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: ap-pli-CA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：ap-pli-CA-tion。

abstract.en: See cream spread thin across a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象乳霜在手上抹开。

abstract.en: See a student bent over one page for hours.
abstract.cn: 想象学生伏案数小时。

examples.en: Her application arrived before the deadline.
examples.cn: 她的申请在截止日期前寄到了。

examples.en: The application of this theory is not simple.

examples.en: A thin application of oil will protect the wood.

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（应用、申请）加 -ation（名词）：申请；应用。

root: 来自拉丁语 applicatio，源于 applicare「贴上、附着」，由 ad 与 plicare「折叠」构成；由「贴上」发展出应用、申请、涂抹与专注等义。

sensesIntro.en: Laying something on gives the request, the use, the smear, and the focused effort.

latinIntro.en: The root plicare, 'to fold', runs through application and complicate.

definition_zh: 申请；应用；涂抹；适用
definition_en: to make a formal request, to put something to use, to spread something on, or to be relevant
core_image: 把一层颜料均匀刷到木板上
scene: 刷墙的师傅把滚筒按进漆里，再一点点推上去。Apply the paint in thin layers.
sceneCN: 这里 apply 是「涂抹」（第 3 个义项：把某物敷到表面）；句意是把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。

pos.zh: 动词：申请；应用；涂抹；适用

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to ask officially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求职位、名额或许可
senses.example: She applied for a place at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了这所学院的一个名额。
senses.why: Latin applicare meant 'to attach oneself to', and a candidate who applies attaches himself to an institution by request.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 意为「使自己附着于」，提出申请的候选人正是用请求把自己附着到某个机构上。

senses.title: To put something to use
senses.definition: to use a rule, method, or idea in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情形中使用规则、方法或观念
senses.example: He applied the same method to a harder problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他把同样的方法用到更难的题上。
senses.why: The original image is laying one thing onto another, so applying a method is laying it onto a case.
senses.whyCN: 本来的意象是把一样东西贴到另一样上，所以 apply 一个方法就是把它贴到一个情形上。

senses.title: To spread something on a surface
senses.definition: to put a substance such as paint or cream onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把颜料、乳霜等物质涂到表面上
senses.example: Apply the paint in thin layers.
senses.exampleCN: 把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。
senses.why: This is the most physical sense and the closest to the Latin verb's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这是最物理的义项，也最接近拉丁语动词的字面含义。

senses.title: To be relevant to
senses.definition: to concern or be valid for a person or case
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某情形有关，或对其有效
senses.example: The ban applies to all vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 这项禁令适用于所有车辆。
senses.why: If a rule can be laid onto a case, the rule reaches that case, which is the intransitive sense with to.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条规则能贴到一个情形上，这条规则就触及该情形，这就是与 to 连用的不及物用法。

intro.en: Apply comes from Latin applicare, 'to attach', and keeps that physical core.
intro.cn: apply 来自拉丁语 applicare「附着」，至今保留这个物理核心。

items.en: plicare meant 'to fold'.

items.en: applicare meant 'to fold to, put against'.

items.en: aplier carried the verb into English.

items.en: Apply first meant 'to attach or put one thing to another'.

items.en: The request sense grew from attaching oneself to an employer or school.
items.cn: 申请义从「把自己附着到雇主或学校」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the apply family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of use and request.
note.cn: 形近组是 apply 词族；近义组是其他表示使用与请求的动词。

normalIntro.en: Apply is laying one thing onto another, in work, in paint, or in a request.
normalIntro.cn: apply 就是把一样东西贴到另一样上，无论是工作、颜料还是请求。

normal.en: Apply for a job, apply to a company.
normal.cn: 职位用 apply for，公司用 apply to。

normal.en: Apply to also means be relevant to.
normal.cn: apply to 还可表示「适用于」。

normal.en: Apply oneself means work hard.
normal.cn: apply oneself 意为专心努力。

normal.en: The past tense is applied, with a single l.

normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPLY。

senses.title: An arranged meeting
senses.definition: a fixed time and place to meet someone

senses.example: I have an appointment with the dentist at four.

senses.why: Appointment is appoint plus -ment, and the older sense of appoint was 'to settle a time', so the noun first named the settling and then the meeting fixed.

senses.title: The act of naming to office

senses.example: Her appointment as head of school surprised nobody.

senses.title: A post or office

definition_zh: 欣赏；感激；理解；领会；增值
definition_en: to recognize the value of something, to be grateful for it, to understand a situation, or to rise in value
core_image: 在画前站定，慢慢看出笔触的好
scene: 他在旧画前站了很久，才看出颜色之间的关系。You learn to appreciate good design slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 appreciate 是「欣赏」（第 1 个义项：认识到某物的价值）；句意是好的设计要慢慢学会欣赏。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：感激的；有欣赏力的
动词：贬值，与 appreciate 相对

senses.title: To recognize the value of something
senses.definition: to see and enjoy the good qualities of something
senses.definitionCN: 看出并享受某物的优点
senses.example: You learn to appreciate good design slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 好的设计要慢慢学会欣赏。
senses.why: Latin appretiare meant 'to set a price on', from ad and pretium, 'price'; to appreciate is first to value a thing rightly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appretiare 意为「给……定价」，由 ad 与 pretium「价格」构成；appreciate 首先就是正确估量一件事物的价值。

senses.title: To be grateful for
senses.definition: to feel thankful for something someone has done
senses.definitionCN: 对别人所做的事心怀感谢
senses.example: I really appreciate your help with the report.
senses.exampleCN: 非常感谢你帮忙做这份报告。
senses.why: If you place a high value on a kindness, gratitude follows naturally, so the valuing sense produced the thanking sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果你把别人的好意估得很高，感激就自然产生，所以「估值」义衍生出「感谢」义。

senses.title: To understand fully
senses.definition: to be aware of how serious or important something is
senses.definitionCN: 意识到某事有多严重或多重要
senses.example: I appreciate that the decision was difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 我理解这个决定很难做。
senses.why: Valuing a situation properly requires seeing it clearly, which is why appreciate also means to grasp a fact.
senses.whyCN: 要恰当估量一个处境，必须先看清它，因此 appreciate 也有「领会事实」的意思。

senses.title: To rise in value
senses.definition: to increase in worth over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移价值上升
senses.example: The house has appreciated since they bought it.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子自他们买下以来已经增值。
senses.why: The price root shows through most plainly here: the thing's price has gone up.
senses.whyCN: 「价格」词根在这里最直白：这件东西的价格上去了。

items.en: The senses of enjoying, thanking, and rising in price all developed from that estimate.

normal.en: I appreciate your help is the standard polite thanks.

normal.en: Appreciate that introduces an understood fact.

core_image: 沿着小路一步步走近山脚
scene: 天色暗下来，远处那盏灯越来越清楚。The train slowed as it approached the station.
